Follow for a new health or science clip every day ⚡

If you shake a sleeping person, they wake up — they can reclaim their consciousness. If you shake a person in a coma or someone under general anesthesia, they don't. That reversibility is the single most important word in the scientific definition of sleep, because it proves sleep is a dynamic, active state the brain can exit on command if the stimulus is strong enough. Which makes sleep a suspension of consciousness, not a loss of it.

Source: "Sleep Isn't Peaceful—Here's What's Really Going On" by Somno Science (YouTube)
https://www.youtub

candidates.title: Income Elasticity Formula Explained | Where Does Y/Q Come From? #Shorts
candidates.description:
Ever wondered where the **Y/Q** term comes from in the formula for Income Elasticity of Demand?

We begin with the basic formula:

Income Elasticity = % change in Quantity Demanded / % change in Income

And then derive the mathematical expression:

**Ey = (Y/Q) × (dQ/dY)**

In this Short, understand the mathematics behind the Income Elasticity formula, rather than simply memorising it.

Simple Mathematics for Economists, explained by Economics with HB.

Minimal pairs are two words that differ in only one sound in the same position and have different meanings. For example, cat and bat differ in their initial consonant sounds, /k/ and /b/. This concept helps linguists identify phonemes and understand how sound differences can change meaning.

Spinal nerves are the peripheral nerves that emerge from the spinal cord and carry both sensory and motor information.

Anterior (ventral) root – pure motor
Posterior (dorsal) root – pure sensory
Spinal (dorsal root) ganglion – sensory cell bodies
Spinal nerve – mixed nerve (31 pairs)
Posterior ramus – back muscles & skin
Anterior ramus – limbs & trunk
Key takeaway:
Lesion of the posterior root → pure sensory loss (dermatome)
Lesion of the anterior root → pure motor loss (myotome)
Lesion of the spinal nerve or rami → mixed deficit

candidates.title: Anselm's Proof and the Perfect Island | Philosophy
candidates.description:
In 1078, Anselm of Canterbury tried to prove that God exists from a definition alone.

Define God as “that than which nothing greater can be conceived.” A being that exists in reality is greater than an idea. So God must exist, Anselm argued.

The monk Gaunilo answered with a parody: the perfect island. By the same logic, it must exist too.

Whether Anselm's reply succeeds is still debated, nearly 1,000 years on.

A chemical reaction that turns rust into molten iron!

क्या आपने कभी सोचा है कि इंसान को पहली बार कैसे पता चला कि पृथ्वी के बाहर एक विशाल अंतरिक्ष मौजूद है? 🌌

candidates.title: How Does Your Brain Remember Things?
candidates.description:
Why do you remember a childhood song but forget someone's name? 🎵

Memory is not a camera that records everything equally. Information competes for attention, gets encoded in different ways and is retrieved with the help of cues.

Repetition, meaning and context can make some memories easier to access. That's why actively recalling something may help more than simply rereading it again and again. Sleep also matters for learning and memory.

Forgetting a detail does not automatically mean something is wrong. Often, what matters is how the information was first noticed and practiced.

On the map Norway looks like a thin strip of land, yet it has one of the longest coastlines on Earth. The mainland coast is about 25,000 km. Add almost 240,000 islands and it grows to more than 100,000 km, enough to circle the planet two and a half times. The reason is the fjords, carved by Ice Age glaciers. The longest, the Sognefjord, is over 200 km long and more than 1,300 m deep. The closer you measure, the longer the coast gets, and that's the coastline paradox.

In Japanese, sun + moon = ... bright? ☀️🌙

Many kanji are built from smaller kanji:

☀️ 日 (sun) + 🌙 月 (moon) = 明 → bright (akarui)
🌳 木 (tree) + 木 (tree) = 林 → woods (hayashi)
🌲 木 + 木 + 木 (three trees) = 森 → forest (mori)
😴 人 (person) + 木 (tree) = 休 → rest (yasumu)
💪 田 (field) + 力 (power) = 男 → man (otoko)
🐦 口 (mouth) + 鳥 (bird) = 鳴 → chirp (naku)
🔥 火 (fire) + 火 (fire) = 炎 → flame (honoo)

These are popular ways to remember the kanji. The real history of some characters is a little different.

Which kanji would you build? 👇

candidates.title: The 10,000 Steps Rule Came From a Product Name #anthropology #animation #cartoon #motivation #fan
candidates.description:
In 1965 a Japanese company called Yamasa put a small clip-on step counter on the market. They named it Manpo-Kei — "ten thousand steps meter" — and sold it with the slogan "let's walk ten thousand steps a day."

 

That is where the number comes from. Not a study. A product name.

 

Sixty years later it sits inside your watch, your phone and your insurance app, and it still feels like medicine. Researchers have since measured walking properly, and the benefits do not switch on at exactly ten thousand.

 

The number was never wrong. It was just never measured.

Scientists study Blood Falls because life like this could exist on Mars or under the ice of Jupiter’s moon Europa.

Sometimes the strangest alien world is right here

📧 For example: thousands of emails labeled “Spam” or “Not Spam” → the algorithm finds patterns → a trained model → predicts whether a new email is spam.

The basic idea:

Data → Learning → Model → Prediction

And that’s Machine Learning.

This is one of the foundations of modern AI — and we’re breaking it down from zero, one concept at a time.

candidates.description:
The quantum model of the atom: why atoms don't collapse
If electrons orbited the nucleus like planets, the circling charge would give off light, lose energy and spiral in. Every atom would collapse in about 16 trillionths of a second.
But an electron isn't a tiny ball. It's a wave, and a trapped wave can only take certain shapes, like a string's notes or a drum's patterns.
Around a nucleus those patterns are three-dimensional: the orbitals 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d.
Squeeze the wave tighter and its energy rises, so the lowest pattern is a floor the electron can't fall through: −13.6 eV, at 0.053 nm.

candidates.title: Why the first second always feels longer #science #neuroscience #explained
candidates.description:
Look at a clock with a second hand. That first second always seems to hang there a beat too long.

👁️ Getting your eyes to the clock takes a saccade — a fast jump — and your brain turns the picture down while your eyes are moving. That leaves a gap of missing footage.

🕐 Rather than show you the gap, your brain backdates the first thing you land on and fills the missing interval with it. So the stretched second isn't your imagination: you really were shown that image for longer than a second.

⏱️ It's called chronostasis, and the stretch is small — measurements put it at up to roughly a tenth

candidates.title: these spinning circles are drawing a bass clef 🎼
candidates.description:
The outline of a bass clef, sampled at 2048 points, is a sum of spinning circles: z(t) = ∑ cₖ eⁱᵏᵗ, with the cₖ from its discrete Fourier transform.

Circle k has radius |cₖ| and turns k times per lap. Keep only the N biggest circles and the widest gap to the outline is 35.3% of the bass clef's height at N = 2, 12.1% at N = 8, 2.2% at N = 32, 0.49% at N = 128 and just 0.12% at N = 512.

The two dots are separate shapes, so the circles draw the clef as one continuous line and hop across to each dot and back: the short straight strokes are those hops.

candidates.description:
No sign of awareness. Why ask her to play tennis?

In 2006, scientists asked a woman diagnosed as being in a vegetative state to imagine playing tennis, inside a brain scanner. Her brain responded like the brains of healthy volunteers, though not everyone agreed on what it meant. In 2024, a study of 353 patients found that about 1 in 4 of those who could not respond to commands showed brain activity suggesting they understood instructions. That doesn't mean every unresponsive patient is aware, and a blank scan doesn't prove someone isn't.

candidates.title: Are Microtubules the Seat of Consciousness?
candidates.description:
Most biologists look at microtubules and see scaffolding. A few researchers see the mind.

Microtubules are tubes about 25 nanometers across that run through every neuron. They give the cell its shape and carry cargo along their length. In the Orch-OR theory of Stuart Hameroff and Roger Penrose, they do something more.

candidates.title: Did the Indian Bride always wear Red?  #history #indianhistory #ancient
candidates.description:
Red is the colour of the Indian bride today. But the old texts tell a different story. The Rigveda gives the bride blue and red. The Harivamsha dresses Rukmini in blue the night before her wedding. Kalidasa puts Parvati in white, with red only on her feet. Rajyashri wears a red veil. Damayanti is in white silk. For over 2,000 years, red marked the bride's feet, forehead and veil, not always her clothes.

What colour did the brides in your family wear? Tell us in the comments.

Sources: Rigveda 10.85.28 · Harivamsha, Vishnu Parva 60 · Kumarasambhava 7.19, 7.26 · Harshacharita ch. 4 · Malatimadh

candidates.title: Why Is This Country Stuck Inside Senegal? 🌍 #geography #facts #shorts
candidates.description:
Gambia is a sliver of land surrounded by Senegal, defined entirely by the path of the Gambia River.

This geography is the result of 19th-century colonial rivalry, where British and French interests fought for control over the river and the surrounding territory. The country acts as a narrow corridor cutting into Senegal, a shape dictated by how far upriver naval vessels could effectively patrol and claim land during that era.

candidates.title: Why does a V8 sound like THAT? 🔊#engineering #gaming #physics #pixelart #engineeringexplained #retro
candidates.description:
Play this V8 + get its full soundtrack → link in bio 🎮🎧

A V8 fires a bang every quarter turn, perfectly evenly. But its crank is a cross, so each side's exhaust gets its 4 bangs unevenly. Two pipes, two lopsided rhythms: that IS the rumble. (A flat-plane crank alternates the sides evenly, and the rumble's gone.)

🎮 V8 LAB: swap the firing order, flip the crank, hear the beat change, rev it till it breaks
🎧 THE FULL V8 SOUNDTRACK: this beat, 2 minutes long
👉 Both at the link in bio · 8bitengineering.org

Why does music have 12 notes? #musictheory #music #math #circleoffifths #shorts
candidates.description:
Twelve notes wasn't a choice - it's a near-miss. Stack pure 3:2 fifths and after twelve of
them you *almost* land back where you started.

The gap is the Pythagorean comma, about a quarter of a semitone. Equal temperament hides it
by shaving ~2 cents off every fifth - so every piano you've heard is slightly out of tune,
on purpose.

Addiction isn't a lack of willpower. It's a real change in the brain. 🧠

Here's what actually happens:

Something can seem obvious to us and still be confusing to someone else. The way we respond can make them comfortable asking another question or embarrassed to admit they’re lost. That matters, because a nod doesn’t always mean the message got through. Helping someone understand takes patience, but also a willingness to explain things differently instead of expecting everyone to think like us. Before getting frustrated that someone doesn’t understand, it’s worth asking: have we explained it in a way that makes sense to them?
